criteria.evidence: The attached file did not exist in the replay environment; after the emulated user said to skip it, the replay located the PR's local commits ('61c61139 Address PR review findings on cross-repo explain', '37e0fbdf Add cross-repo checkpoint explain') and continued from that context.
The replay never stated the PR URL; the user supplied 'https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1915' in turn 3 and the replay's replies (turns 2-4) do not include it.

Replay still calls remote.FetchCheckpointRefFrom into the cwd repo ('write the canonical ref name ... and made the write temporary instead'), then reverts the ref; objects remain ('Fetched objects stay in the object store unreferenced'), and the fetch-on-miss fallback is untouched — the cwd repo is written to, not left unchanged.

TestCrossRepoExplain_FetchAndRender passes for prose, but resolution works precisely because the ref is stored locally during the command (borrow-then-revert), not looked up without storing; no export-mode (--json/--transcript) coverage added.

'go build ./... clean, gofmt clean'; 23 failures in cmd/entire/cli shown identical before/after and on main (hooksPath/no-origin environment); mise and golangci-lint not installed and the replay said so.

judge.reason: The replay implemented a borrow-and-revert of the foreign ref in the cwd repo rather than a pure lookup, so the cross-repo flow still writes the foreign ref and objects into the local repo and leaves the fetch-on-miss path intact, failing c3 and the 'without storing it locally' clause of c4. It also never provided the PR URL itself (c2), while build/tests were handled acceptably given the environment.
